items.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Conte Candoli, we were the two babies in the band, the two young kids.

ctx.x: And Jackie and Roy were on the band?

Oh yes. I would put his popularity at that time on a par with Chick Corea at his zenith, or any other group that you know had a zenith couple of years, you know what I mean by that? He was in a sense a very hot attraction. He was definitely a jazz band but he had that commercial tinge by the two kids singing the doodley, doodadly, beedeley vocals. And we would open like the Chicago State Theater, I mean we would be THE not opening act, we would be the closing act there, which was a very big theater, or any of the…
Absolutely. And he still sounds good, too.

items.title: Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, 1997
items.q: You mean everybody’s there — Snooky, Conte and Shaughnessy and all the cats are all there?

ctx.x: I can recall Johnny sitting there, and looking over there, and saying your name, and he knew all the guys in the band.

Yeah. He was great. I’ll tell you what, he was a very personal, private person. But, when it come to the band, he was very protective of us, man. He would always come and listen to us rehearse, and he knew every one of us, and always went out of his way to be good to us. You know very few people ever got to see his home, and where he lives. The band did. Absolutely. He was a great guy. I haven’t seen him in the last couple or three years. I know about two or three years ago, when Doc and the band, we go out and…
